script: My ex‑boss ruined Jacob's legacy—now I am exposing his cruel betrayal.. I signed my ex‑boss up for a St. Jude donation email in honor of the guy he'd written up and later died from cancer. I was working under my ex‑boss, Dale, who was the absolute bane of my days. Jacob, the manager who hired me, was the only decent guy in that mess. He'd been upfront, praised us, and said the whole corporate thing ran because of us. Two years in, Dale got hired. He was the kind of guy who had a reputation for being a pain in the ass across the whole company. Dale had the authority to write up anyone, and he did it to Jacob for the dumbest things—wrong paint shade, leaving early, even minor things that never happened before. Jacob had never been written up in his whole career. He was close to retiring and even joked about quitting to work at McDonald's just to escape the toxicity. HR sided with Dale, saying Jacob made it up. When Jacob fell asleep during an interview, Dale put him on temporary leave and hired a replacement—an 18‑year‑old with zero experience. The new manager was a woman named Kathy, who had no background in our department but was hired because her office was next to Dale's. She gave us nonsensical projects and made us work longer than needed. We knew Dale would fire Jacob whether it was a health issue or not. A month later, after scans and bloodwork, Jacob was diagnosed with lymphoma that had spread to his brain. He died a day or two after the diagnosis. It broke our hearts. I was angry. So I went to St. Jude's cancer research page, signed up to donate monthly to lymphoma research, and chose to do it in honor of Jacob. I used his work email and address so Dale would get the thank‑you email. I didn't care if Dale canceled the subscription; I just wanted him to see the single email thanking him for the donation in Jacob's name. Later, I bought a pinned Asian blue bee with a paper that says "bee thoughtful" to remind everyone to be kind to people going through tough stuff. (That's the tea, bestie.)
